title: Love Me, Love Me Not
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Shy, romance-dreaming Yuna and practical Akari become friends when they turn out to live in the same apartment building. Yuna falls for Akari's stepbrother Rio, who secretly loves Akari, while Akari grows close to Yuna's childhood friend Kazuomi. Io Sakisaka's Shogakukan Award-winning shojo follows four teens sorting out love, friendship and family across high school.
life_message: Honesty with yourself and consideration for friends let love mature, even through rejection.

content.note: Teen crushes, confessions, kisses; Rio's feelings for his stepsister (Wikipedia; MU Stepsibling/s).
Inferiority and suppressed feelings (MU Inferiority Complex).
Rio initially dates girls only for looks (MU).

dominant: Coming-of-age romance; friendship as moral center

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Four peers; parents in the background.

folkways.japan: Shared apartment-building neighbors, formal love confessions (kokuhaku) and restraint about stating feelings reflect Japanese school-romance norms.

delivery.evidence: No review or summary in the sources describes delivery; style inferred from premise and tags (to verify).
delivery.note: Its view of love is carried by the four teens' choices rather than by stated lessons.

winners_losers: Everyone ends paired and growing (Yuna with Rio, Akari with Inui per Wikipedia); the story sympathizes with honest self-reflection.
